subject: Signal Sled — evaluation success criteria & acceptance runway
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@zenwell.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Signal Sled — evaluation success criteria & acceptance runway

Claire — thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a lightweight MAP (signal-sled-MAP.xlsx) and a companion acceptance-tests.md that translate the objectives we discussed into measurable checks. High level proposal below; the MAP contains owner assignments and a suggested 4-week cadence.

Summary (proposal):
- Evaluation window: 4 weeks (target start: 2026-08-20)
- Primary success axis: production-like quality + predictable unit economics
- Key measurable criteria (pass = all must be true):
  * Functional: end-to-end integration test pass rate >= 98% (daily smoke)
  * Quality: Intent / classification F1 >= 0.92 on the 250-sample benchmark set
  * Latency: p95 generation latency <= 220ms for 512-token requests on the dedicated test pool
  * Throughput: sustained 120 req/s for peak workload profile with <5% error rate
  * Security/Compliance: SOC2 evidence upload + contractual data residency confirmation

Exit gates (examples in MAP):
- Soft gate (midpoint): stable integration and quality signals for 7 consecutive days (no regression >2% F1)
- Hard gate (final): acceptance tests and SLA checklist signed by Zenwell eng + Redwood AE/SE

Acceptance tests (attached acceptance-tests.md) include: onboarding API sanity, concurrency stress harness, sample prompt concordance, rollback/resilience check, and evidence bundle for SOC2/KMS.

Ask: Please review the MAP and acceptance-tests attachment; confirm owners or propose edits by EOD 2026-08-16 so we can lock the start date. If that works, I’ll schedule weekly 30-min syncs (Tuesdays) and share a read-only Results Drive for test artifacts.

Attachments: signal-sled-MAP.xlsx (MAP with owners & timeline), acceptance-tests.md (test definitions)

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the fast turnaround and clear draft. A few clarifications from our side before we finalize:

1) Data residency: we need confirmation that logs and ephemeral inputs for the trial will remain in us-east-1; can Redwood provide the KMS key ID and the SOC2 evidence bundle you mentioned? (we've attached our evaluation checklist.)

2) Quality benchmark: the F1 >= 0.92 target looks reasonable, but can you add a breakdown by intent category (triage / patient-verification / scheduling)? We have three critical intents where recall matters more.

3) Latency vs cost: our product team is sensitive to p95 latency spikes during batch windows. Can you document expected token cost per response and an estimated cost delta for the dedicated test pool vs hosted API?

4) Who on Redwood will own the canary rollback plan if the trial shows a regression? We want a named on-call in the MAP.

If we can get answers on those four bullets and the SOC2 evidence by Monday EOD (2026-08-16), we can lock the internal approvals and start on 2026-08-20.

Attachment: zenwell-eval-reqs.pdf (Zenwell obs/constraints)

Best,
Claire Hsu
Director, Product Ops | Zenwell Health
claire.hsu@zenwell.com

Claire — hi, Ben here (SE). Addressing your bullets and adding concrete acceptance test definitions so the MAP can be locked:

1) Data residency / SOC2 / KMS
- We will provision the evaluation infrastructure in us-east-1 and use a customer-scoped KMS envelope key. KMS Key placeholder: redwood:us-east-1:rk-zenwell-demo (we'll provide the full ARN in the evidence bundle).
- SOC2 excerpt will be pushed to the Results Drive; acceptance gate requires receipt of the SOC2 PDF and confirmation from your security contact.

2) Quality breakdown by intent (we'll include categories in the benchmark CSV):
- Triage (N=100): target recall >= 0.94
- Patient verification (N=75): target F1 >= 0.93
- Scheduling (N=75): target F1 >= 0.90
- Overall: weighted F1 >= 0.92

3) Latency & cost estimate (example load profile in MAP):
- p95 generation latency <= 220ms (512-token baseline) on the dedicated test pool. If you choose lower-latency routing, p95 may improve to ~180ms at ~1.25x token cost.
- Estimated token unit cost (trial config): ~0.6 microcredits/token (dedicated q4-int8). Full cost spreadsheet in MAP tab "Economics".

4) Canary / rollback owners and playbook:
- On-call: Ben Carter (primary), Jordan Blake (backup).
- Rollback policy: automatic fallback to hosted-compat model after 5 consecutive error spikes >3% or a regression >3% F1 on the probe set.

Acceptance tests (short):
- API onboarding: API key auth + sample call -> 100% success
- Sanity prompt concordance: 250 sample prompts -> overall pass if daily drift <2%
- Concurrency stress: 120 req/s sustained for 10 minutes, errors <5%
- Failover test: introduce artificial node failure, system recovers within 90s and no data loss
- Evidence bundle: SOC2 PDF, KMS ARN, ephemeral log retention policy (7 days)

Next steps: Naomi will add the intent-tagged benchmark CSV into the MAP and update owners. If Zenwell approves these gates, we propose kickoff 2026-08-20 and a mid-eval checkpoint on 2026-08-27 to review smoke results.

I can assemble the evidence bundle this weekend. Claire — can you confirm Zenwell's security reviewer (name/email) so I can share a secure link?

Attachments: acceptance-tests.md (updated with intent breakdown)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
